cur:catacombs-arles-concordius.summary: Under a lid carved with small scenes and an inscription, Christ sits enthroned at the centre of an arcaded colonnade, surrounded by the apostles seated in pairs on either side. The ordered, symmetrical composition presents Christ as the heavenly ruler and teacher of the apostolic college.
facts: The museum dates it to 380/390; it is carved from Carrara marble.
Commons has a separate photograph of the inscription on its lid, from which the sarcophagus takes the name of Concordius.
cur:catacombs-arles-concordius.notes: The apostles are not individually identifiable in the photograph.

cur:catacombs-bargello-raising-of-lazaru.summary: Within a ring of gold triangles, Christ raises Lazarus beside a tree; the gold figures are partly obscured by corrosion. The scene of Lazarus, the most frequent Gospel miracle in catacomb art, made this an apt object to set beside a Christian grave.
facts: The Bargello catalogues it as Roman, about 350–400, showing the raising of Lazarus.
Such gold-glass medallions survive mostly because they were embedded in the plaster sealing catacomb tombs.
cur:catacombs-bargello-raising-of-lazaru.notes: Surface damage makes the details hard to read; the identification follows the museum.
